newsitem.title: USA: Consolidated Freightways to spin-off units.
newsitem.headline: Consolidated Freightways to spin-off units.

text.p: Consolidated Freightways Inc said on Monday that it plans to spin-off its long-haul, less-than-truckload units.
Consolidated Freightways Inc, which has revenues of $5.7 billion said it will spin-off the new company, to be called Consolidated Freightways Corp, to shareholders in a tax-free transaction.

The units to be spun off have revenues of about $2.1 billion and include CF MotorFreight and its Canadian operations, including Canadian Freightways Ltd, Epic Express, Milne & Craighead and Canadian Sufferance Warehouses.

Donald Moffitt, chairman, president and chief executive officer of Consolidated Freightways Inc will continue in those positions at CNF Transportation, while W Roger Curry, president and chief executive officer of CF MotorFreight, will head the new Consolidated Freightways Corp.
Moffitt said the changing face of the transportation industry brought about the spin-off.

"These changes, which have been especially dramatic in the past 18 months, have increasingly placed our separate and distinct regional and national trucking companies in a position where they are in direct competition with each other," he said in a statement.
"This spin-off appropriately addresses these changes," he added. Moffitt said the two companies would be more competitive as independant companies.
